title: Expand buffer cache and align planner I/O costs to cut physical reads
configuration_cause: shared_buffers=16384 (128MB) is tiny versus 2.1TB RAM; blks_read_per_txn=1.51 vs blks_hit_per_txn=9.23 (~14% miss) and effective_io_concurrency=1 with random_page_cost=4.0 make the planner overvalue physical random I/O, inflating GetUserTweets terminal occupancy (0.885).
mechanism: The dominant GetUserTweets transaction consumes 88.5% of terminal capacity with p50=196us and 1.51 physical block reads per txn against only 9.23 hits. A 128MB shared_buffers cannot retain the hot tweet/user working set, so each lookup pays a random read. Raising shared_buffers to 1GB, raising effective_cache_size to reflect the 2.1TB host, enabling prefetch (effective_io_concurrency) and lowering random_page_cost/seq_page_cost together let the planner prefer cached index paths and the buffer pool retain hot pages, reducing per-transaction read latency and terminal occupancy.
query_effect: Cached index lookups for GetUserTweets replace random physical reads; planner favors index scans over seq scans on hot relations.
expected_tps_effect: Increase successful_transaction_tps by reducing GetUserTweets terminal occupancy.

predictions.rationale: Larger buffer pool retains hot pages, cutting random reads per lookup.
More cached pages reduce physical block reads per transaction.
Lower per-transaction read latency frees terminal capacity for more completions.

alternatives.statement: If buffer expansion does not move blks_read_per_txn, the residual is WAL sync latency (sync_average_ms=0.131) and the next action should target the wal_commit_path bundle instead.
If blks_read_per_txn falls but TPS does not rise, the bottleneck is planner cost misestimation rather than cache capacity, isolating random_page_cost/seq_page_cost as the effective lever.

why_exceeds_incumbent: Incumbent leaves shared_buffers at 128MB despite a 2.1TB host and a 14% buffer miss rate on the dominant transaction; the coherent cache bundle directly attacks the measured low_buffer_hit_ratio anomaly that drives GetUserTweets terminal saturation.

knob_changes.numerical_basis: 1GB = 131072*8kB; 8x current, well within safe range 8192-65536... capped at 65536
4GB estimate, upper safe bound; host has 2.1TB RAM
16 concurrent prefetch requests, modest step from 1 within 0-256
Slight reduction to keep ratio consistent; within 0.5-2.0
knob_changes.mechanism_role: I/O cost scale paired with random_page_cost

nodes.label: Hot pages retained, fewer physical reads

edges.relation: raises cache hit ratio and lowers per-txn reads
lower read latency frees terminal capacity
